intervals.label: Phase I construction
intervals.note: Mirrors experiment:mu3e (same lower-bound reasoning). Start is a lower bound, not a stated "construction began" date: the earliest dated source found that calls Phase I "under construction" is the December 2018 European-Strategy submission (arXiv:1812.06540v1, 16 Dec 2018), whose own Mu3e section says "Construction of the Mu3e Phase-I experiment will begin in 2019" (a plan). PSI's news list shows a construction meeting in Wengen on 01.03.2019 and the solenoid arriving on 29.07.2020. Phase I was still described as "currently under construction" in the June 2026 abstract (Phi-Psi 2026) and on 16.09.2026 the fourth pixel layer was still to follow for the next beam time, so the interval stays open.
intervals.quote: The first phase of the Mu3e experiment is under construction at PSI

intervals.label: 2026 installation of the central detector station
intervals.locator: psi.ch/en/mu3e/news: 10.07.2026 vertex detector, 07.08.2026 fibre detector, 21.08.2026 tile detector, 16.09.2026 layer 3, 24.09.2026 craned into the PiE5 area
intervals.note: Phase annotation (kind phase). End: Today Mu3e was craned from the staging setup to the PiE5 area, where the experiment was inserted into the Mu3e magnet. (24.09.2026).
intervals.quote: Mu3e has installed the vertex detector for the 2026 beamtime, marking an important milestone in the detector assembly.

name: Mu3e detector
notes: The technology class is 'other': none of the listed classes names a silicon-pixel HV-MAPS tracker specifically; Mu3e's tracker is solid-state silicon, not a gas TPC, so 'gaseous_tpc' does not fit.

summary.plain: A very thin, high-speed silicon camera built from custom pixel chips, combined with fast timing detectors, being assembled at the Paul Scherrer Institute to catch three particles flying apart from a single muon.
summary.technical: Multi-layer HV-MAPS silicon pixel tracker (vertex + outer tracking layers; third layer installed 2026-09) combined with scintillating-fibre and scintillating-tile timing systems, on the PSI HiMB/piE5 beamline. Under construction; no data yet.

technology.quote: To this aim, we use innovative high-voltage monolithic active pixel sensors (HV-MAPS)
technology.value: Ultra-thin silicon pixel tracker built from high-voltage monolithic active pixel sensors (HV-MAPS), combined with scintillating-fibre and scintillating-tile timing detectors
